description: Second source-backed booster focused on tourism, wildlife, heritage, art/craft, food and Jharkhand identity for broader query experiments.

entities.name: Betla National Park
entities.description: Betla National Park in Latehar district is part of the Palamau tiger landscape and is known for forest, wildlife and historic fort remains.

entities.name: Dalma Wildlife Sanctuary
entities.description: Dalma Wildlife Sanctuary near Jamshedpur is a forested hill sanctuary strongly associated with elephants and trekking.

entities.name: Netarhat
entities.description: Netarhat is a hill destination in Latehar district known for its plateau scenery, cool climate, sunrise and sunset viewpoints.

entities.name: Magnolia Sunset Point
entities.description: Magnolia Sunset Point is a popular sunset viewpoint near Netarhat.

entities.name: Koel View Point
entities.description: Koel View Point near Netarhat overlooks the Koel river valley.

entities.name: Parasnath Hill
entities.description: Parasnath Hill in Giridih is one of the most important Jain pilgrimage landscapes and is also sacred in local tribal tradition.

entities.name: Maithon Dam
entities.description: Maithon Dam is a major Damodar Valley Corporation project on the Barakar River near Dhanbad.

entities.name: Topchanchi Lake
entities.description: Topchanchi Lake is an artificial reservoir and picnic destination in Dhanbad district surrounded by hills and forest.

entities.name: Panchet Dam
entities.description: Panchet Dam is a multipurpose Damodar Valley Corporation dam on the Damodar River near Dhanbad.

entities.name: Pahari Mandir
entities.description: Pahari Mandir is a Shiva temple on a hill in Ranchi reached by a long staircase and especially visited during Shravan.

entities.name: Jagannath Mandir Ranchi
entities.description: Jagannath Mandir at Jagannathpur in Ranchi is a historic hilltop temple known for its annual Rath Yatra.

entities.name: Deori Mandir
entities.description: Deori Mandir near Tamar on the Ranchi-Jamshedpur route is an old stone temple with both tribal Pahan and Brahmin worship traditions.

entities.name: Chhinnamastika Temple Rajrappa
entities.description: The Chhinnamastika temple at Rajrappa in Ramgarh district is a major Shakti shrine near the confluence of the Bhairavi and Damodar rivers.

entities.name: Basukinath Dham
entities.description: Basukinath Dham near Jarmundi in Dumka district is a major Shiva pilgrimage site with a large Shravan-season gathering.

entities.name: Saranda Forest
entities.description: Saranda is an extensive Sal forest landscape in West Singhbhum, traditionally associated with the Ho community and elephant habitat.

entities.name: State Museum Hotwar
entities.description: The State Museum at Hotwar, Ranchi presents archaeology, ethnology, art and cultural heritage of Jharkhand.

entities.name: Sohrai and Khovar Art
entities.description: Sohrai and Khovar are traditional wall-art practices of Jharkhand using locally available natural earth pigments and distinctive motifs.

entities.name: Paitkar Painting
entities.description: Paitkar is a traditional scroll-painting practice associated particularly with Amadubi in East Singhbhum.

entities.name: Dokra Craft
entities.description: Dokra is a traditional metal-casting craft made through the lost-wax process and practiced by artisan communities in Jharkhand.

entities.name: Thekua
entities.description: Thekua is a wheat-based sweet snack made with sugar or jaggery and is strongly associated with Chhath offerings.

entities.name: Til Barfi
entities.description: Til Barfi is a sesame-and-jaggery sweet associated with winter and Makar Sankranti in Jharkhand.

entities.name: Bamboo Shoot
entities.description: Bamboo shoots are used as a local vegetable ingredient in Jharkhand cuisine.

facts.evidence: Latehar district administration lists Betla National Park as a district tourist destination.

facts.value: The wider Palamau-Betla landscape became one of India's early tiger-reserve areas in 1974.
facts.evidence: The district tourism page describes Betla's early tiger-reserve history.
The district page identifies the cooler November-March period as a suitable visiting season.

facts.value: Forest wildlife, waterfalls, hot springs and historic fort remains are part of the broader visitor experience.
facts.evidence: The district page highlights wildlife and surrounding natural/historic attractions.
East Singhbhum district presents Dalma Wildlife Sanctuary as a major attraction near Jamshedpur.

facts.value: The Dalma hills rise to around 3,000 feet.
facts.evidence: The district tourism description notes the sanctuary's hill elevation around 3,000 feet.

facts.value: Elephants are strongly associated with the sanctuary; other wildlife and many bird species also occur there.
facts.evidence: Jharkhand forest/tourism material identifies Dalma as important elephant habitat with diverse wildlife.

facts.value: Trekking and nature exploration are common visitor activities.
facts.evidence: District tourism material promotes outdoor activities in the Dalma hills.
Latehar district lists Netarhat as a principal tourist destination.
The district tourism page gives Netarhat's elevation at roughly 3,622 feet.
The official district page places Netarhat roughly 156 km west of Ranchi.
Netarhat's official tourism description emphasizes its scenic sunrise and sunset experience.

facts.value: About 10 km from Netarhat bus stand
facts.evidence: Latehar district tourism material places Magnolia Point around 10 km from Netarhat bus stand.
Magnolia Point is promoted as a sunset-view destination.

facts.value: About 2 km from Netarhat bus stand
facts.evidence: Latehar tourism information places Koel View Point about 2 km from the bus stand.

facts.value: Overlooks the Koel river valley below Netarhat
facts.evidence: The official tourism listing describes the Koel river visible from the viewpoint.
Giridih district lists Parasnath as a major district tourist and pilgrimage site.

facts.value: Jains know the pilgrimage landscape as Sammed Shikhar/Shikharji; tradition associates it with liberation of twenty Tirthankaras.
facts.evidence: The Giridih tourism page explains Parasnath's importance in Jain tradition.
The official district description notes the hill's significance to local Santhal tradition as Marang Buru.
Dhanbad district describes Maithon Dam as built across the Barakar River.
The district page gives Maithon's approximate distance from Dhanbad.

facts.value: Damodar Valley Corporation multipurpose project with hydroelectric generation
facts.evidence: The official tourism description identifies the DVC project and underground hydel station.
Dhanbad district describes Topchanchi as an artificial lake/reservoir.
The official tourism page reports an area of about 214 acres.

facts.value: About 37 km from Dhanbad railway station
facts.evidence: The district tourism page provides the distance from Dhanbad railway station.
Dhanbad district identifies Panchet as a dam on the Damodar River.
The district page gives Panchet's approximate distance from Dhanbad.
The official tourism page gives 1959 as the dam's inauguration year.
Ranchi district identifies Pahari Mandir as a Shiva temple.
The district page notes the stairway used to reach the temple.

facts.value: Especially busy during the Shravan month
facts.evidence: Ranchi tourism information highlights Shravan as an important visiting period.
The district tourism page dates the Ranchi Jagannath temple to 1691.
Ranchi district credits Ani Nath Shahdeo with construction of the temple.
The temple is especially known for its annual Rath Yatra.

facts.value: Deori village near Tamar on the Ranchi-Jamshedpur route
facts.evidence: Ranchi district tourism places the temple near Tamar on the highway corridor.

facts.value: Old stone construction traditionally described as interlocked without conventional binding material
facts.evidence: The official tourism description highlights the temple's unusual stone construction.

facts.value: Both tribal Pahans and Brahmin priests participate in worship
facts.evidence: The district page notes the coexistence of Pahan and Brahmin worship traditions.
Ramgarh district lists Rajrappa among its principal tourist destinations.

facts.value: Bhairavi River meets the Damodar River
facts.evidence: The district tourism page describes the river confluence at Rajrappa.

facts.value: Major Shakti shrine dedicated to Chhinnamastika
facts.evidence: Ramgarh district describes the Chhinnamastika temple as the central pilgrimage attraction.
Dumka district tourism places Basukinath near Jarmundi.
The official district page identifies Basukinath as a Shiva pilgrimage temple.

facts.value: Large pilgrimage gathering during Shravan, especially July-August
facts.evidence: Dumka tourism information highlights the Shravan mela/pilgrimage season.
Government material locates Saranda in the West Singhbhum forest landscape.

facts.value: Extensive Sal forest spread across a landscape of many hills
facts.evidence: Government material describes Saranda as a vast Sal-forest and hill landscape.

facts.value: Ho tribal communities are closely associated with the Saranda landscape
facts.evidence: Official material notes the presence and cultural association of Ho communities with Saranda.
